official.deadline_note: Fixed annual deadlines: 15 August for the autumn semester and 1 February for the spring semester. The scholarship form is only released in the portal from 15 June (autumn) or 1 December (spring), and applications may be submitted no earlier than two months before the deadline. The German page adds a technical note that the autumn-2026 form was only accessible from 10 July.
official.application_cycle: Spring semester 2027 round (next); standing cycle with fixed autumn (15 August) and spring (1 February) deadlines
official.status_note: No closing of the current round is published. Submission deadlines are fixed and recurring, the office reviews applications continuously after each deadline, and the next scholarship deadline is 1 February 2027 for the spring semester.
benefits: Scholarships generally do not need to be repaid; repayment is only required in exceptional cases such as false information or unreported changes in financial circumstances.

Scholarships are paid for the entire semester, credited to your account about one week after the approval decision, and may arrive as several payments depending on which foundation(s) you are assigned to.
Scholarship holders can apply for a waiver of the UZH/ETH Language Center's course fees with the office's letter of acceptance.
The office submits applications to various foundations on your behalf at no cost, in order to increase your chances.
Long-term financing is pursued where there are no significant changes to your financial situation or academic performance, though there is no legal entitlement to it.
Inflation adjustment of the scholarship amount was decided by the university executive board and has been implemented from 2025 onwards.
eligibility: We only support first degree programmes at every level of study, and we do not support PhD study programmes.

Income limit: CHF 86,000 of taxable income and CHF 300,000 in net worth (federal tax assessment); the income limit increases by CHF 6,000 for each additional child who is completing their initial education.

Eligibility by residence category (official overview PDF): Swiss nationals and C-permit holders from the start of studies; EU/EFTA and non-EU/EFTA B-permit Bachelor's students after 55 ECTS credits; Master's students only if they hold a Swiss Bachelor's degree; Master's students without a Swiss Bachelor's degree are not eligible.
A personal asset exemption of CHF 5,000 per person is granted; anything above this is considered in the calculation. Earnings up to CHF 6,000 per year do not reduce the scholarship.

If your grades at UZH are very good you can apply for support already after your first semester; with protection status S you need 55 ECTS, at least 20 ECTS per semester and a grade point average of at least 4.5.

Incoming mobility students are not supported. Support is supplementary to cantonal scholarships, parental contributions under Art. 276-277 SCC and your own income; refugees and stateless people may apply.
requirements: A UZH email address is required to access the application form; if it has not been received two weeks before the deadline, contact the office.
Documents must be formatted as PDF and uploaded one document per upload; applications and attachments cannot be sent by email.
The most recent tax return from you and your parents.
The latest available final tax assessment from you and your parents; provisional tax assessments must not be submitted.
If you do not file a tax return in Switzerland: account statements for all your bank accounts from the past 6 months.
A motivation letter of about one A4 page for a first application, or a semester report of about one A4 page for a subsequent application, each dated and signed by hand.
documents: Motivation letter (first application), about one A4 page, dated and hand-signed
Semester report (subsequent application), about one A4 page, dated and hand-signed
Most recent tax return of the applicant and of the parents
Latest available final tax assessment of the applicant and of the parents
Account statements for all bank accounts of the past 6 months, if no Swiss tax return is filed
Proofs of social security benefits such as children's pensions; recommendation letters only if expressly requested
selection_criteria: Objective financial need, checked against documentation of your financial situation and that of your parents.
Academic performance, which is also relevant to the decision.
The mission of the private foundations the office applies to on your behalf; which foundation(s) you are assigned to is decided solely by the Student Financial Aid Office.
Completeness of the file: the earlier your application is submitted in full, the sooner it will be processed.
There is no legal entitlement: the private foundations are free to grant scholarships or not.
coverage: Supplementary support where the assessed need is not covered by the parents, the students themselves or with state funds.
The office assumes that a single person without children needs around CHF 12,000 per semester, and bridges the gap where less than this is at your disposal.
Contributions to health costs can be paid out in special situations.
In 2024 the office granted roughly CHF 1.5 million in support to 206 people, mostly as non-repayable social scholarships.
application_method: The entire application process is handled via a single online portal.
In the portal you can upload documents and track the current status of your application.
If an application is submitted successfully, you will receive a confirmation by email.
Approvals or rejections are communicated directly via the portal as downloadable documents, with a notification to your UZH email address.
Applications and supporting documents cannot be sent by email; students with visual impairments are asked to make contact.
official.application_route: Apply through the UZH single online application portal, which requires a UZH email address; the form is only available in German and opens about two months before the 15 August (autumn) or 1 February (spring) deadline.
official.citizenship_residency: Swiss nationals and C-permit holders are eligible from the start of studies. EU/EFTA and non-EU/EFTA B-permit holders are eligible for a Bachelor's programme only after 55 ECTS credits, and for a Master's programme only if they hold a Swiss Bachelor's degree; Master's students without a Swiss Bachelor's degree are not eligible. Refugees and stateless people may apply. The student loans (regular, hardship and Pecunia) require Swiss citizenship or a C permit.
official.international_eligibility: Yes, but restricted: international Bachelor's students become eligible after 55 ECTS credits (or after the first semester if their UZH grades are very good), international Master's students are eligible only if they hold a Swiss Bachelor's degree, and incoming mobility students are not supported at all.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No subject restriction. The office applies on your behalf at various foundations and selects them according to their mission; applicants cannot choose which foundation they are assigned to.
official.duration: Granted per semester and paid for the entire semester; long-term support over the course of the degree is pursued where the financial situation and academic performance remain stable.
official.description: The Student Financial Aid Office of the University of Zurich supports enrolled students in first degree programmes at every level of study whose financial need cannot be covered by their parents, their own income or state funding. Support is granted in cooperation with private foundations, primarily in the form of non-repayable scholarships and sometimes as loans, on a subsidiary basis. The office checks whether you are objectively in need, and only supports first degree programmes, not PhD study.
official.program_type: Means-tested supplementary university scholarship (social scholarship), granted in cooperation with private foundations

not_confirmed: funding_amount and funding_period: the office states that the amount 'depends on your income and other factors' and publishes no fixed award figure. The only official figure is the assessed need of CHF 12,000 per semester for a single person without children, which is the budget basis, not the award itself.
tuition_coverage and study_mode: the pages carry no wording stating that tuition or semester fees are paid from the scholarship, and no study-mode statement.
english_requirement: no English test or medium-of-instruction rule is published for this funding.
travel_coverage: no travel, relocation or installation allowance is published.
verification.notes: Verified the English and German FAQ, the application and deadlines page, the Bachelor's/Master's/Prospective student support pages, the tuition and living-cost page, the 'Study Funding at UZH - Overview' eligibility PDF and the 2024 annual report. No award amount is published, so none is recorded. applicant_utility.summary: This is a needs-tested top-up, not a full ride: the office only closes the gap that remains after your parents' legally required contribution, your own earnings and any cantonal scholarship, so the strongest files are the ones with a documented shortfall rather than simply low income. You cannot pick a foundation, and there is no legal entitlement, because the decision sits with private foundations acting on their own mission. International applicants face the sharpest timing trap: Bachelor's students generally need 55 ECTS before they can apply at all, Master's students need a Swiss Bachelor's degree, and the form itself is only in German.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Enrolled UZH students on a first degree programme (Swiss and C-permit holders from day one, international Bachelor's students after 55 ECTS) whose parental taxable income is under CHF 86,000 and who cannot cover Zurich living costs from other sources.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are on a first degree programme: PhD, a second Master's or a Master's without a Swiss Bachelor's are all out of scope.
Secure your UZH email address at least two weeks before the deadline, because without it the portal form cannot be opened.
File your and your parents' Swiss tax returns early and do not request an extension at the tax office.
Draft the one-page motivation letter (first application) or semester report (renewal), date it and sign it by hand.
Convert every attachment to PDF and rehearse a cache-cleared private browser window before the deadline day.
Use the phone consultation hours, Monday and Thursday 14:00-15:00, for a non-binding pre-check of an unclear situation.
common_rejection_risks: An incomplete file: review of attachments happens first, and processing only runs once the file is complete, so missing papers push the decision well past the 8-10 week window.
Parental taxable income above CHF 86,000 or net worth above CHF 300,000, where only CHF 6,000 per sibling in initial education buys headroom.
Household assets above the CHF 5,000 per-person exemption, including saved or inherited money.
Applying at the wrong level or with the wrong permit status, especially international Master's students without a Swiss Bachelor's degree.
Sending provisional tax assessments instead of the latest final one.
Assuming you will be matched to a foundation of your choosing, or that an earlier approval sets a precedent for the next round.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and semester fees, the share of the roughly CHF 2,200 per month Zurich living baseline that exceeds your assessed need, and for non-EU/EFTA students the CHF 21,000 visa proof or a Swiss guarantor; the additional costs of dual-degree programmes are explicitly not covered by scholarships.
document_audit: Two tax papers are needed, not one: the declaration you filed plus the latest final tax assessment, for both you and your parents.
With no Swiss tax return, supply six months of statements for every bank account you hold, including foreign ones.
Declare all accounts as one net CHF figure in the form, and show any leftover scholarship money from the previous semester separately in the remarks field.
Uploads are one document at a time and only count when the green bar appears; uploaded files stay invisible in the portal until staff have checked them.
Unsolicited recommendation letters are ignored, so only forward one if the office has expressly asked for it.
Parents unwilling to share their paperwork can send it directly to the office without you seeing it.
alerts: Loans are closed to you unless you are a Swiss citizen or hold a C permit, so international students have no loan fallback.
Incoming exchange and mobility students receive no support from this office at all.
The portal form opens only about two months before each deadline, so start organising documents a month ahead and clear your browser cache before logging in.
International Bachelor's students effectively lose their first year: 55 ECTS is the normal threshold, and only very good grades unlock an earlier, possibly reduced, award.
Non-EU/EFTA students must separately evidence CHF 21,000 or a Swiss guarantor for the visa, which this award does not discharge.
Apply even while a cantonal decision is still pending, because the cantonal award can be added into the calculation afterwards.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Open the UZH portal, complete the German web form, upload the PDFs one at a time before the deadline, then watch the portal: the decision lands as a downloadable document roughly 8-10 weeks after the deadline, with payment credited about a week after approval.
